entry.title: Transitioning from SAP Business One to SAP Cloud ERP
entry.content:
Advancing from SAP Business One to SAP Cloud ERP — What Growing Companies Should Consider

SAP Business One has helped thousands of small and midsize businesses establish control, visibility, and efficiency across finance, sales, purchasing, and inventory. For many organizations, it has been a reliable and practical foundation for years. 

But as businesses grow—expanding into new markets, increasing transaction volumes, or diversifying operations—questions begin to emerge: 

  • Can our ERP scale with us? 
  • Are we able to access real-time insights across the business? 
  • How quickly can we adapt to changing requirements?
  • What will it take to support the next phase of growth? 

For companies asking these questions, SAP Cloud ERP becomes increasingly relevant—not as a replacement for what has worked, but as a next step to support what comes next. 

This post explores why SAP Business One customers begin evaluating SAP Cloud ERP, what value it can bring, and how to approach a transition with clarity and confidence.  

Why SAP Business One Customers Reassess Their ERP Landscape 

SAP Business One is designed to be straightforward, efficient, and cost-effective. However, growth-oriented organizations often reach a stage where new demands introduce additional complexity: 

  • Expanding into multiple countries or legal entities 
  • Managing higher transaction volumes and operational scale 
  • Navigating evolving regulatory and reporting requirements
  • Integrating with a growing ecosystem of applications 
  • Delivering faster, more data-driven decisions 

At the same time, expectations around technology are changing. Business users increasingly expect intuitive experiences, embedded analytics, automation, and seamless connectivity across systems. 

As a result, what once felt simple and sufficient can begin to feel limiting—not because SAP Business One is inadequate, but because the business itself has outgrown its original requirements. 

SAP Cloud ERP enters the conversation as a way to support this next phase—offering a modern, scalable foundation designed for continuous change without added complexity.  

How SAP Cloud ERP Supports Growing Businesses 

For organizations evaluating SAP Cloud ERP, the most important question is not “What features does it offer?” but “How will it improve how we operate?” 

Customers transitioning from SAP Business One frequently highlight several key benefits: 

  • Continuous Innovation 
    SAP Cloud ERP delivers regular updates with new functionality, eliminating the need for disruptive upgrade cycles. Businesses can adopt innovations as they become relevant rather than planning large-scale system changes. 
  • Scalable, Standardized Processes 
    SAP Cloud ERP is built on proven best practices that help standardize operations across finance, procurement, sales, and supply chain. At the same time, it allows flexibility where differentiation matters. 
  • Real-Time Visibility 
    Analytics are embedded directly into business processes, enabling faster decision-making with up-to-date, integrated data—rather than relying on separate reporting tools or delayed insights. 
  • Automation and Intelligence
    Routine, manual tasks can be automated, allowing teams to focus on higher-value activities such as analysis, planning, and customer engagement. 
  • Reduced IT Complexity
     Infrastructure, system maintenance, and updates are managed by SAP, reducing the operational burden on internal IT teams and enabling them to focus on innovation instead. 

For many SAP Business One customers, these advantages translate into improved agility—the ability to respond faster to opportunities and challenges as the business evolves.  

Addressing Common Questions from SAP Business One Customers 

Transitioning to a new ERP system is a significant decision. SAP Business One customers typically raise several practical questions when considering SAP Cloud ERP. 

  1. Is transitioning from SAP Business One complex or disruptive? 
    A transition does require planning, but it doesn’t need to be disruptive. Many organizations take a structured approach—reviewing existing processes, cleaning and organizing data, and then implementing in phases aligned with business priorities. 
  2. What happens to our existing processes? 
    SAP Business One systems often reflect years of process refinement. Moving to SAP Cloud ERP presents an opportunity to simplify and standardize where possible. Many existing processes can be mapped to standard cloud best practices, reducing complexity while preserving what works. 
  3. Will we lose flexibility? 
    Not at all. While SAP Cloud ERP emphasizes standardization, it also supports extensions and integrations that allow businesses to maintain differentiation without complicating the core system. 
  4. How long does the transition take? 
    There is no universal timeline. The duration depends on factors such as organizational readiness, data quality, and scope. The most successful transitions align the roadmap with business goals rather than treating it as a purely technical implementation. 
  5. Can SAP Cloud ERP integrate with our other systems? 
    Yes. SAP Cloud ERP is built for integration, making it easier to connect with other SAP solutions, third-party applications, and modern digital platforms. 

 What Customers Experience After Moving to SAP Cloud ERP 

While every journey is different, common outcomes emerge across organizations that have transitioned from SAP Business One to SAP Cloud ERP. 

  • Simplified Core Operations
    Standardized processes across finance and operations reduce complexity and make it easier to scale as the business grows. 
  • Faster, More Informed Decisions 
    Real-time access to data improves visibility across the organization, reducing reliance on manual reporting and enabling quicker responses. 
  • Less Time Spent on Maintenance
    With technical operations managed in the cloud, IT teams can shift focus from system upkeep to supporting business innovation. 
  • Improved User Experience 
    Modern, intuitive interfaces help drive adoption across the organization, improving productivity and engagement. 
  • Greater Readiness for Growth 
    Perhaps most importantly, companies position themselves to expand—with an ERP foundation that can adapt as they evolve. 

These outcomes reflect a broader shift: ERP becomes less about managing transactions and more about enabling business performance.  

How to Approach the Transition 

Every SAP Business One customer starts from a different place, which is why there is no one-size-fits-all path. However, several steps can help set a strong foundation: 

  • Assess your current system: Understand how SAP Business One is being used today—across processes, data, and integrations. SAP has enabled an automatic scope suggestion in its Digital Discovery Assessment (DDA) for the functionality that is in use in your SAP Business One system. This provides a head start in analyzing and deciding on the scope of your SAP Cloud ERP system. Learn more:
     https://discovery-center.cloud.sap/missiondetail/4724/5008/. 
  • Identify growth drivers: Align the ERP transition with your strategic objectives, whether that’s expansion, efficiency, or innovation. 
  • Simplify where possible: Use the transition as an opportunity to reduce complexity and standardize processes. 
  • Plan in phases: Break the journey into manageable steps that minimize disruption while delivering value early. Know that SAP provides tools to support your transition. For example, Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) tools help ease the effort required for migrating data into the SAP Cloud ERP system. Learn more:
     https://discovery-center.cloud.sap/missiondetail/4639/4928/ 
  • Leverage expertise: Work with experienced partners and SAP resources to guide the process and reduce risk. For example, SAP can guide you with a proven transition methodology and best practices. Learn more:
     https://me.sap.com/roadmapviewer/group/658F507A-D6F5-4B78-9EE1-0300C5F1E40F/roadmapoverviewpage/2669d3902b244345ac1f9586ab433d73. 

The goal is not to move quickly—it’s to move deliberately, with a clear understanding of what success looks like for your organization.  

Taking the Next Step 

If you are currently running SAP Business One and beginning to think about your next stage of growth, exploring SAP Cloud ERP is a natural step. 

SAP has created a dedicated transition page that is a great place to get started. 

A transition doesn’t need to be rushed. But early planning helps ensure that your ERP landscape evolves in step with your business—supporting innovation, scalability, and resilience over the long term. 

For many organizations, advancing to SAP Cloud ERP is not about replacing what works today. It’s about building a stronger foundation for tomorrow.

entry.title: Getting Support for SAP Business One: Clear Steps and Where to Start
entry.content:
A practical guide for customers and partners 

If you are an SAP Business One customer or partner and something does not work as expected, knowing how to get help – and what happens after you raise a request – can make the support experience much smoother. SAP Business One follows a clear, partner‑led support model designed to keep customers closely involved while ensuring issues are handled through the right channels. Read on to find out how it all works! 

How SAP Business One Support Works 

SAP Business One is sold, implemented, and supported through SAP‑certified partners. Customers work directly with their partner, while SAP provides the support platform, tools, and escalation paths in the background. All SAP Business One support activities are handled through the through the Support Launchpad for SAP Business One, which is used by both customers and partners.

 

Step 1: Contact Your SAP Business One Partner 

Your SAP Business One partner is always the first point of contact for support. The partner understands your system's landscape, configuration, and add‑ons, and can often resolve issues quickly. Providing clear details such as error messages, screenshots, and business impact will help speed up resolution. 

Step 2: Partner Review and Investigation 

After you raise an issue, your partner investigates the root cause. Many topics can be resolved at this stage through configuration changes, known corrections, or best‑practice guidance. If SAP involvement is required, your partner takes care of sending the case to SAP Support. 

Step 3: Using the Support Launchpad (Customers Have Access Too) 

When an issue needs SAP support, your partner creates a case in the Support Launchpad for SAP Business One. Customers can also access the same Launchpad to track cases, view status updates, search SAP Notes and knowledge articles, request license keys, and manage S‑users and system data

Important: SAP Business One support does not use SAP for Me. Business One has its own dedicated support processes, and the Support Launchpad remains the central tool for both customers and partners. 

Step 4: SAP and Partner Collaboration 

Once a case is logged, SAP works directly with the partner to analyze and resolve the issue. Your partner remains in your main contact and ensures communication stays clear and consistent. Customers can stay informed by following progress in the Support Launchpad and through updates shared by their partner. 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

 

Customer vs Partner – At a Glance

Here is a summary of who does what during the SAP Business One Support Process

 

Customer Partner 
  • Contact your SAP Business One Partner for Support 
  • Act as the first point of contact 
  • Provide issue details and business impact 
  • Investigate and troubleshoot issues 
  • Track your support cases in the SAP Business One Launchpad 
  • Create and manage support incidents 
  • Search SAP notes and knowledge base articles 
  • Send cases to SAP when required 
  • Request SAP Business One License Keys 
  • Coordinate resolution with SAP 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                

Additional Support Resources 

Please see guidance on how to access the Support Launchpad for SAP Business One here. 

Check out the following for more information on the support process: 

SAP Business One Support Overview 

2951753 - How to get Support for SAP Business One - SAP for Me 

3325732 - When do Business One customers use SAP Business One Support Launchpad vs. SAP for Me? - SAP for Me 

2388701 - How can SAP Partners get technical support for SAP Business One? - SAP for Me 

Summary 

Getting support for SAP Business One follows a clear and predictable path: customers work with their partner, partners investigate and send cases to SAP when needed, and SAP provides deeper‑level support through defined processes. By using the same Support Launchpad, customers and partners benefit from shared visibility, transparency, and a consistent support experience. 

  SAP Business One 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

Thank you for reading!  

We hope you found this helpful. Please note that the Customer Interaction Center is always happy to guide you on any of the mentioned processes and assist you with any queries you may have! 

You can contact CIC for assistance if you need any further guidance. The Customer Interaction Center can be contacted by Phone, Expert Chat and by email.

entry.title: Practical AI in SAP Business One: from business questions to better decisions
entry.content:
For many SMEs, the most valuable AI opportunities are also the most practical: finding answers faster, reducing repetitive work and making better decisions.

The challenge is turning that potential into something genuinely useful.

AI can generate responses quickly. But business decisions rarely depend on a single piece of information or a simple answer. They depend on context – understanding the situation behind the question.

Why did sales drop?
Which customers need attention?
What’s affecting profitability?
How could a change in regulations impact operations?

The usefulness of AI depends on whether it can understand the business context behind those questions.

SAP Business One brings together the data and processes businesses rely on every day. By connecting AI with that context, SAP Business One creates new ways for people to explore their business – from asking questions more intuitively, to understanding what’s happening, to applying AI in more specialised scenarios.

Helping people find answers more naturally

Every business has questions. The challenge is often getting from the question to the answer.

Traditionally, exploring business data could require knowing which report to run, understanding how information is structured or asking someone with technical knowledge to create a database query.

That creates a gap between the people who understand the business question and the tools needed to answer it.

AI User Defined Query in SAP Business One helps close that gap.

Instead of writing a database query, users can describe the question they want to answer using everyday business language. AI User Defined Query tool, powered by SAP AI Core Services, generates the SQL script needed to retrieve the relevant data, which users can review before running it.

The process brings together the strengths of AI and human judgement: AI helps create the query, while users remain in control of reviewing the request and the results. At no point does AI directly access company data which is entirely secure.

But the real value is what happens next.

The results open in List View, where users can filter, sort and analyse the information further. Instead of producing another static report that answers one question and ends there, the results become a starting point for investigation.

A question leads to another question. A pattern leads to a deeper investigation.  If desired the List View can then be saved for future investigations.

The people closest to the business can explore what’s happening themselves, without needing to rely on someone else to prepare the answer.

 

From understanding what happened to exploring why

Business data tells a business what’s happening.

But many decisions require a wider perspective.

A change in regulations could affect operations. A shift in market conditions could influence demand. A supplier issue could require understanding factors beyond your own transactions.

Many AI experiences start with a blank prompt. Before AI can help, users need to explain the situation, provide the background and describe what they are trying to understand.

Ask AI in SAP Business One takes a secure approach, powered by the same SAP AI Core Services that supports AI User Defined Query

Using Ask AI, users can bring selected SAP Business One context into their question, combining business information from within SAP Business One with AI-based internet research. The user controls which field values and context are shared, while AI uses that context to provide a more relevant response. At no point does the AI gain direct access to the company database, and it knows only the specific data shared within the context of the question asked. 

The difference is subtle but important. Instead of asking a general question and then explaining why it matters, users can start with the business situation they are already exploring.

That makes AI usage secure and more useful for questions where internal business data is only part of the answer.

 

From everyday improvements to specialist capabilities

The most useful AI applications will look different for every business.

Some use cases will be straightforward: automating repetitive work, reducing manual steps or improving consistency in processes where accuracy matters.

Others will be more niche: capabilities designed around particular industries, roles or business scenarios.

That’s why SAP Business One is designed to support both built-in AI capabilities and further innovation through SAP and partner solutions.

SAP AI services can support scenarios such as document processing and automation, while SAP Business One extensibility enables partners to build additional AI solutions using SAP technologies. See the AI Partner Innovations Playbook for SAP Business One.

This creates a broader ecosystem where businesses can apply AI in the areas that matter most to them – whether that’s a common business need or a specialist capability for a particular market.

Making AI work for the people who know the business best

AI doesn’t replace the institutional knowledge that exists within a business.

The people closest to customers, suppliers, products and operations are often the ones asking the most salient questions. The opportunity is to give them better ways to explore those questions, understand what’s happening and act on what they discover.

SAP Business One brings AI closer to those everyday decisions.

By connecting AI with business context, it helps businesses move from simply having access to AI to using AI in ways that are practical, relevant and valuable.

For businesses, that means more opportunities to use AI not as a separate technology, but as part of how they understand their operations, respond to change and pursue new opportunities.

See It in Action

entry.title: Managing SAP AI Core using PowerShell
entry.content:
Why a PowerShell GUI for SAP AI Core?

SAP AI Core is the backbone of SAP's generative AI runtime. It hosts orchestration deployments, manages resource group isolation, and serves AI capabilities across SAP applications and custom workloads. In addition to the capabilities available in SAP AI Launchpad, there is often a need for a scriptable interface to perform common lifecycle operations programmatically, including resource group management, deployment administration, status inspection, and resource cleanup.
 

This PowerShell Code Sample is a single .ps1 file that opens a native Windows Forms GUI. It connects to the SAP AI Core REST API using a service key you paste in at launch. Credentials are held in memory only and are never written to disk.

Prerequisites

What You Need Before You Start

You need an active SAP AI Core service instance with at least one service key, and a Windows machine with PowerShell 5.1 or later.

Requirement Details

SAP BTP AccountGlobal account with entitlement for SAP AI Core (extended plan required)
SAP AI Core Service InstanceCreated in a Cloud Foundry space; plan: extended
Service KeyAt least one service key on the instance — you will copy the JSON credentials
Windows 10 / 11PowerShell 5.1 ships built-in; no additional runtime needed
Execution PolicyRun Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned if scripts are blocked
 
New to SAP AI Core? Use the Set Up Account for SAP AI Core booster in SAP BTP Cockpit. It creates a subaccount, assigns entitlements, provisions the service instance, and generates a service key in four guided steps.

Getting Connected

Connecting to SAP AI Core

When you launch the script, a Connect to SAP AI Core dialog opens immediately. All you need is the JSON from your SAP AI Core service key.

Step 1 — Copy the Service Key JSON from BTP Cockpit

Navigate to your subaccount in SAP BTP Cockpit, go to Services → Instances and Subscriptions, open your SAP AI Core instance, click the service key name under Credentials, and click Copy JSON.

SAP BTP Cockpit — Credentials dialog for the SAP AI Core instance. Click "Copy JSON" to copy the service key to the clipboard.


Step 2 — Launch the Script and Paste Your Credentials

Right-click SAP AI Core PowerShell Code Sample.ps1 and choose Run with PowerShell, or open a PowerShell window and run .\SAP AI Core PowerShell Code Sample.ps1. The Connect dialog appears. Paste the JSON into the SERVICE KEY JSON text area and click Connect (or press Ctrl+Enter).

Connect dialog on first launch — paste your service key JSON here.
 
Security note: The JSON is parsed into in-memory variables (clientId, clientSecret, tokenUrl, aiApiUrl). Nothing is persisted to disk. Clicking Disconnect clears all variables from memory.

 

Resource Groups

Managing Resource Groups

Resource groups are the primary isolation boundary in SAP AI Core. Each one gets its own namespace for configurations, deployments, artifacts, and secrets. After connecting, the Resource Groups tab loads automatically.

Resource Groups tab after connecting — the "default" resource group is shown as PROVISIONED.

Creating a New Resource Group

Click + New Resource Group. An inline form expands above the list. Enter a Resource Group ID (lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens only). The Document Grounding checkbox is available if your tenant supports it and defaults to disabled.

New Resource Group form — enter an ID and optionally enable Document Grounding, then click Create Resource Group.

Click Create Resource Group. New groups appear in PROVISIONING status first, then move to PROVISIONED within seconds once the namespace is ready on the cluster.

Other Actions

  • Refresh — re-queries /v2/admin/resourceGroups and repaints the grid.
  • Delete Selected — prompts for confirmation, then deletes the selected resource group.
  • View JSON — shows the raw API response for the selected row, including labels and metadata.

 

Configurations

Orchestration Configurations

An orchestration configuration links a resource group to the SAP AI Core orchestration scenario. Every deployment is based on a configuration, so you need at least one per resource group before you can deploy.

Switch to the Configurations tab and select a resource group from the dropdown. The grid loads all configurations scoped to that group.

Configurations tab — the "orchestration" configuration listed with its scenario, executable, and configuration ID.

Creating a New Configuration

Click + New Configuration. The inline form has three fields:

  • Resource Group — pre-selected from the dropdown.
  • Configuration Name — defaults to orchestration, the recommended value matching the SAP AI Core orchestration scenario.
  • Version — defaults to 0.0.1.

The Scenario and Executable fields are locked to orchestration — the only valid values for the orchestration scenario on the extended plan.

New Orchestration Configuration form — name defaults to "orchestration", scenario and executable are locked.

Click Create Configuration. The list refreshes automatically. Select the new row and click Deploy Selected to create a deployment from it — the tool switches to the Deployments tab automatically.

 

Deployments

Deployments

The Deployments tab shows all deployments for the selected resource group, including deployment ID, current status, target status, configuration ID, and last modified time.

Deployment in PENDING status immediately after creation — target status is RUNNING.
 
 
Deployment transitions to RUNNING — the orchestration endpoint is live.
 

Lifecycle Actions

Action When Available API Call

StopDeployment is RUNNINGPATCH /v2/lm/deployments/{id} with targetStatus: STOPPED
ResumeDeployment is STOPPEDPATCH /v2/lm/deployments/{id} with targetStatus: RUNNING
DeleteAny state (prompts confirmation)DELETE /v2/lm/deployments/{id}
View JSONAlwaysGET /v2/lm/deployments/{id} — full API response
Tip: Click Refresh after a Stop or Resume action. SAP AI Core processes lifecycle changes asynchronously — a deployment may briefly show PENDING before reaching its target state.

Get Started

Download and Run

The sample is distributed as a single ZIP containing SAP AI Core PowerShell Code Sample.ps1. No installation, no dependencies beyond what ships with Windows.

 
  1. Download the ZIP
    Unzip SAP AI Core PowerShell Code Sample.zip to any folder.
  2. Allow script execution (once, per user)
    Open PowerShell and run: Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned
  3. Run the script
    Right-click SAP AI Core PowerShell Code Sample.ps1 → Run with PowerShell, or from a terminal: .\SAP AI Core PowerShell Code Sample.ps1
  4. Paste your service key and connect
    Copy the credentials JSON from SAP BTP Cockpit, paste it into the dialog, and click Connect.

Ready to Try It?

Download the script, connect with your service key, and manage your SAP AI Core resources from the desktop in under two minutes.
Download PowerShell Code Sample

See and end-to-end video how to use this in context with SAP Business One

entry.title: From Any Source to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Complete SAP S/4HANA Migration Cockpit Guide
entry.content:
In almost every S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition project data migration is the longest and often underestimated workstream, that causes the most stress closest to go-live. The questions are always the same: which approach do we use, what can be migrated?

This blog tries to answer all of this in one place by using SAP S/4HANA Migration Cockpit, accessible via the SAP Fiori Migrate Your Data app as the thread. Whether you're coming from - a non-SAP legacy system, SAP ERP, or SAP Business ByDesign or SAP Business One - there is a defined path and knowing it upfront saves a lot of effort later.

 

Which Approach Is Right for You? Quick Decision Guide

Before diving into the details, here's the short version:

Your Current SystemMigration ApproachKey Consideration
Non-SAP / custom SAP ERPStaging TablesBroadest migration object coverage; data prep effort is highest
SAP ERPDirect TransferCoverage of available migration objects is lower, streamlined
SAP Business ByDesignStaging TablesBuilt-in extraction tool available for data preparation and transformation for most objects
SAP Business OneStaging TablesQueries for Data extraction and tools for data transformation provided for key objects on Business Accelerator Hub

If your source system is in that table, read the relevant section below. If you're evaluating multiple options, read all four.

 

The Shared Starting Point: Always a New Implementation

Before discussing the differences, the most important, common characteristic should be highlighted: the migration to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition is always a new implementation (greenfield), independent of source system.

There is no system conversion (brownfield), and no selective data transition in the traditional SAP ERP sense if the target is the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Configuration, business processes, and integrations must be (re)built using SAP Best Practices. Only the business data are transferred.

 

Migration from non-SAP /Custom SAP ERP to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Using the Migrate Data Using Staging Tables Approach (aka Staging Tables)

How it works

The SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit creates temporary database tables - staging tables - for each migration object in your migration project. You populate these by uploading data via SAP-provided XML or CSV templates, or by feeding data in directly through ETL tools. Once the data is in staging tables, the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit validates it, lets you apply value mappings, and then transfers it into your S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system.

For more information about the Migrate Data Using Staging Tables: see SAP Help Portal.

What's available

SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition ships with 240 migration objects (CE 2608) for the staging tables approach, covering customers, suppliers, products, AR/AP open items, G/L account balances, and much more.

For available migration objects see: https://help.sap.com/S4_CE_MO - select the migration approach Staging Table.

Ideal Use cases

  • Migrating from non-SAP legacy systems
  • SAP ERP: Where data needs significant cleansing and transformation before load, the available migration object scope of the direct transfer approach is not sufficient, or the SAP system is below SAP ECC 6.0
  • Projects where an ETL tool or partner tooling is used to feed the staging tables

Who is this for?

This approach suits the broadest customer segment: any company moving to S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition regardless of their source system. It is the default choice for net-new cloud customers, companies replacing a non-SAP system, and organizations that need full control over data transformation before it enters the target system.

 

Migration from SAP ERP to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Using the Migrate Data Directly from SAP System Approach (aka Direct Transfer)

How it works

Rather than using files, the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit establishes a direct connection to your existing SAP ERP system. Data is extracted from the source and transferred directly into you S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system. This requires that the SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud Edition is based on 3-system-landscape, your source system is an SAP ECC 6.0 and DMIS 2011 SP25+ add-on is installed, and the communication arrangement SAP_COM_0816 is created on the target side (see solution process: BH3 on SAP Signavio Process Navigator)

As of CE2602, SAP introduced optional Staging Tables as Intermediate Storage feature for direct transfer, giving you greater transparency and the ability to review and adjust data before it is transferred to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. This required, in addition, that the communication arrangement SAP_COM_0678 is created. (see solution process 2Q2 SAP Signavio Process Navigator). 

For more information about the Migrate Data Directly from SAP System see: SAP Help Portal.

💡Tip:

  • See blog from Mirella Vorsprach: Migration Cockpit in SAP Cloud ERP 2602
  • See blog from Philipp Kreutzheide: SAP S/4HANA Migration Cockpit – Migrate Data Directly from SAP System – Using Staging Tables

What's available

The direct transfer approach currently covers 24 migration objects (CE2608), fewer than the staging tables approach.

For available Migration Objects: https://help.sap.com/S4_CE_MO - select the migration approach Direct Transfer.

Ideal Use Cases

  • Companies running SAP ECC 6.0 moving to S/4HANA Public Cloud Edition
  • Projects where the required migration objects fall within the supported 24-migration object scope
  • Scenarios where the source data is already well-structured and largely clean
  • Migrations were minimizing manual file handling and reducing transformation effort is a priority

Who is this for?

This approach targets SAP ERP customers making the move to the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. It is common in the mid-market and in subsidiaries of larger SAP customers that run SAP ERP and are now standardizing on SAP Cloud Public Edition.

 

Migration from SAP Business ByDesign to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Using the Migrate Data Using the Staging Tables Approach 

Context

SAP delisted SAP Business ByDesign from its price list for new customers on 20 April 2026. Existing customers remain fully supported, there is no announced end date, but SAP's strategic direction is clear: The successor platform for the mid-market is SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

How it works

Instead, it relies on a file-based / template-driven approach, which maps to the staging tables approach in the S/4HANA migration cockpit. Data is first exported from SAP Business ByDesign using the built-in self-service extraction tool, then mapped and transformed (using the tools provided on Business Accelerator Hub) to match the S/4HANA migration object structure and finally loaded into the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit's staging tables via template upload. From there, the standard migration process runs.

👉 SAP Business ByDesign does not use the direct transfer approach.

💡Tip:

  • SAP provides a dedicated learning path for this scenario: Migrating Data from SAP Business ByDesign to SAP S/4HANA Cloud.
  • See blog from Babu Lal Limba: Data Extraction from SAP Business ByDesign for Migration to Cloud ERP

What's available

The built-in SAP ByDesign extraction tool supports the most common migration objects: master data, transactional data, and accounting data. On the target side, the full set of ~240 migration objects (CE2608) of the staging tables approach in S/4HANA Public Cloud is available.

Ideal Use Cases

  • Companies that have outgrown SAP Business ByDesign functionally and need a more scalable platform
  • Migration of master data (business partners, products,…) and open items from SAP Business ByDesign
  • Projects leveraging the built-in extraction tool to pull data cleanly and structurally from SAP Business ByDesign
  • Strategic consolidations where multiple SAP Business ByDesign tenants are merged into a single S/4HANA instance

Who is this for?

SAP Business ByDesign customers are typically mid-sized companies (50–500 users) who originally chose the cloud-native SAP Business ByDesign for its simplicity and lower TCO. Migration to S/4HANA Public Cloud Edition is the next step for those who have grown beyond SAP Business ByDesign’s functional scope, or who want to align with SAP's long-term platform strategy proactively, ahead of any future support changes.

 

Migration from SAP Business One to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Using the Migrate Data Using the Staging Tables Approach

How it works

For SAP Business One customers migrating to S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, the route is through staging tables approach: data is extracted from SAP Business One, using direct database queries, or partner tooling, mapped to SAP-provided XML migration templates and then loaded into the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit. Because SAP Business One's data model differs significantly from S/4HANA Public Cloud Edition's, the transformation and mapping phase requires particular care. SAP has provided tools to extract and transform the data, for some of the key objects in SAP Business One, into SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition format for upload.

👉 SAP Business One is also not a supported source system for the direct transfer approach.

What's available

On the target side, the full set of 240 migration objects (CE2608) of the staging tables approach in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition is available. There is no native extraction interface from SAP Business One into the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit - data preparation is entirely the responsibility of the customer or implementation partner.

Ideal Use Cases

  • Migration of master data and transactional data from SAP Business One into S/4HANA Cloud Public Editon
  • Projects where partner tooling or custom ETL tools bridge the gap between the SAP Business One data model and S/4HANA structure
  • Consolidations where SAP Business One is replaced by S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition as the central platform

Who is this for?

SAP Business One customers are typically small to mid-sized businesses (up to ~50 users) that have either outgrown the platform or are seeking a more capable foundation for further growth. Migration requires investment in data preparation, but the staging approach gives teams full control over data quality before anything goes live.

 

Key Principles: Regardless of Approach

A few things hold true across all four migration scenarios:

  • The migration cockpit is an initial load tool. It inserts data; it does not update or sync. Migrated records cannot be re-migrated or deleted from the target
  • Historical data (e.g. past invoices, completed orders) cannot be migrated
  • Valid ≠ correct. The migration cockpit will accept values that are technically valid but business-incorrect (e.g. wrong groupings). Value mapping decisions require domain expertise, not just technical mapping
  • Test before you migrate. Run migration tests in a dedicated test system before the productive load.
  • Data quality is a business task, not an IT task. The earlier business stakeholders are involved in data cleansing and sign-off, the smoother the go-live

 

Conclusion

The SAP Fiori Migrate Your Data app (SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit) covers all four scenarios described above. When you understand which path applies to your source system, the project becomes significantly more predictable. The biggest lever in every migration is not the approach itself; it's how early you start assessing data quality and involving the right people.

If you're currently planning a migration project, the first practical step is a data assessment: which objects need to move, how clean the source data is, and which of the available migration objects you need. Everything else follows from there.

💡Tip: For that data assessment step, the SAP Fiori Explore Migration Objects app is exactly the right starting point. It gives you a structured view of all migration objects available for the staging table approach and their dependencies. It also shows which migration objects are assigned to a given scope item.

  • See: Explore Migration Objects - SAP Help Portal
  • See blog from Frank Finkbohner: The New Explore Migration Objects App, The Game Changer in Planning Your Data Migration and What’s New in the Explore Migration Objects App: Releases 2602.4 and 2608
