entry.title: SAP Business One Webhooks via Service Layer — Part 3: Advanced Features and Production Best Practice
entry.content:
Version note: The features require SAP Business One 10.0 FP 2608 or later.

Introduction

Parts 1 and 2 covered the foundational mechanics of webhooks: how they work, how to create and manage subscriptions, how to secure them, and how to monitor delivery. That knowledge is enough to build a working integration.

But working is not the same as efficient. When you subscribe to Orders.Created with a basic subscription, SAP Business One sends you every created order. If you only care about orders above €10,000, or orders from a specific customer group, or orders created during business hours — you are receiving and filtering noise in your own code, after the fact.

Part 3 covers:

  1. BizObjProps — include meaningful business data in the notification payload itself, reducing follow-up API calls
  2. FilterExpr — filter events server-side so irrelevant events never reach your endpoint
  3. The Webhook Formula language — the expression syntax powering FilterExpr
  4. Production best practices — architecture patterns, operational guidance, and a troubleshooting runbook

1. Richer Payloads with BizObjProps

The default payload problem

By default, a webhook notification payload contains only the primary key of the affected record:

{
    "id": "5ac18923-cfce-40d3-a31e-7154ca4d5191",
    "type": "sap.b1.Orders.Created.v1",
    "subject": "91",
    "data": {
        "DocEntry": "91"
    }
}

Knowing that order DocEntry 91 was created is a starting point, but your integration almost always needs more: who is the customer? What is the total? When is it due?

The traditional approach is to make a follow-up call to Service Layer:

GET /b1s/v2/Orders(91)?$select=DocEntry,CardCode,DocTotal,DocDueDate

This works, but it has costs:

  • Extra round-trip latency — every notification requires an additional HTTP call
  • Load on Service Layer — high-volume integrations make many follow-up GET calls per second
  • Timing sensitivity — if the record was updated again between the notification and your follow-up GET, you might not see the state it was in when the event fired

Including extra fields with BizObjProps

BizObjProps lets you specify additional header-level fields to include directly in the data section of the notification payload. You add it to the event entry in EventCollection:

POST /b1s/v2/EventSubscriptions

{
    "WebhookID": "OrdersEnrichedWebhook",
    "WebhookURL": "https://your-app.example.com/webhook/orders",
    "AuthenticationType": "HMAC",
    "AuthenticationCred": "{\"Key\": \"your-secret-key\", \"Algorithm\": \"HMACSha256\"}",
    "Handshake": "tYES",
    "EventCollection": [
        {
            "BusinessObject": "Orders",
            "TransactionType": "Created",
            "BizObjProps": "DocEntry, CardCode, CardName, DocTotal, DocCurrency, DocDueDate, Comments"
        }
    ]
}

The notification payload now looks like:

{
    "id": "5ac18923-cfce-40d3-a31e-7154ca4d5191",
    "type": "sap.b1.Orders.Created.v1",
    "subject": "91",
    "data": {
        "DocEntry": 91,
        "CardCode": "C20000",
        "CardName": "Maxi-Teq",
        "DocTotal": 15000.00,
        "DocCurrency": "USD",
        "DocDueDate": "2026-10-15T00:00:00Z",
        "Comments": "Urgent delivery required"
    }
}

For many integrations, this eliminates the need for any follow-up GET call.

Rules for BizObjProps

Only simple (header-level) properties are allowed. You cannot include collection properties like document lines (DocumentLines), tax lines, or item price lists. Allowing those would cause the payload to balloon in size and create performance problems.

Property names must exactly match Service Layer field names. Case matters. Check the Service Layer metadata or documentation to confirm the correct property name.

BizObjProps is per-event entry. Different events in the same subscription can specify different BizObjProps:

"EventCollection": [
    {
        "BusinessObject": "Orders",
        "TransactionType": "Created",
        "BizObjProps": "DocEntry, CardCode, DocTotal"
    },
    {
        "BusinessObject": "BusinessPartners",
        "TransactionType": "Updated",
        "BizObjProps": "CardCode, CardName, Phone1, EmailAddress"
    }
]

When to use BizObjProps

Use it whenever the integration needs more than just the key to do its job and the extra fields are simple scalar values. Good candidates:

  • Routing logic: "if this order is for customer group X, send it to system Y"
  • Notifications: "alert the sales rep when their customer's order is created"
  • Downstream sync: "replicate these header fields to our CRM without a follow-up call"

Avoid it for:

  • Document line details (use a follow-up GET for those)
  • Very large string fields that would bloat the payload
  • Fields that are slow to compute

2. Smart Event Filtering with FilterExpr

The notification noise problem

Imagine you manage a large SAP Business One company with hundreds of orders per day. Your webhook integration monitors Orders.Created to push data to a fulfillment system — but the fulfillment system only cares about orders above €5,000. Without filtering, you receive every order notification, process it, check if it is above €5,000, and then discard most of them.

This wastes:

  • Network bandwidth (notifications you do not need are still delivered)
  • Endpoint processing time (you still parse and evaluate every event)
  • Queue capacity in the Messenger

FilterExpr solves this: you write a boolean formula that is evaluated against the business object's fields inside SAP Business One, before the notification is sent. Only events where the formula evaluates to true trigger a notification.

Basic example

{
    "BusinessObject": "Orders",
    "TransactionType": "Created",
    "BizObjProps": "DocEntry, CardCode, DocTotal",
    "FilterExpr": "DocTotal > 5000"
}

With this filter, your endpoint only receives notifications for orders with a DocTotal greater than 5000. Orders for smaller amounts are silently ignored.

Combining filter and enrichment

FilterExpr and BizObjProps work perfectly together:

{
    "BusinessObject": "Orders",
    "TransactionType": "Created",
    "BizObjProps": "DocEntry, CardCode, CardName, DocTotal, DocDueDate",
    "FilterExpr": "DocTotal > 5000 && DocDueDate - DocDate < 7"
}

This sends enriched notifications only for large orders that are also urgent (due within 7 days of creation).

Rules for FilterExpr

  • The formula must evaluate to a boolean value (true or false). Non-boolean result → notification is suppressed.
  • Variables in the formula refer to the header-level fields of the business object (same restriction as BizObjProps — no collection fields).
  • The formula is evaluated at event time, against the state of the record at that moment.
  • FilterExpr and BizObjProps are independent — you can use one without the other. But they pair naturally.

3. The Webhook Formula Language

The formula language used in FilterExpr is a purpose-built expression engine. It looks like a mix of JavaScript and Excel formulas. This section covers every feature, with real SAP Business One field examples.

Literals

A literal is a fixed, hardcoded value in your formula.

Type

Examples

Integer

1, 100, -20, 0

Decimal

3.14, 99.99, -0.5

String

'hello', 'C20000', 'USD' (use single quotes)

Boolean

true, false

Variables

A variable refers to a field on the business object being evaluated. Use the exact Service Layer field name.

DocTotal       // the document total
CardCode       // the business partner code
DocDate        // the document date
Confirmed      // a boolean field

You do not declare variables — they are resolved automatically from the business object at evaluation time.

Relational Operators

Compare two values. The result is always true or false.

Operator

Meaning

Example

==

Equal to

CardCode == 'C20000'

!=

Not equal to

DocCurrency != 'USD'

> 

Greater than

DocTotal > 10000

< 

Less than

Discount < 5

>=

Greater than or equal to

DocTotal >= 1000

<=

Less than or equal to

Quantity <= 100

Real SAP Business One examples:

// Only notify for orders above €5,000
DocTotal > 5000

// Only notify when a specific customer is involved
CardCode == 'CORPORATE_KEY_ACCOUNT'

// Only notify for non-zero discounts
Discount != 0

Logical Operators

Combine multiple conditions.

Operator

Meaning

Rule

&&

AND — both must be true

DocTotal > 5000 && CardCode != 'INTERNAL'

||

OR — at least one must be true

DocTotal > 10000 || CONTAINS(CardCode, 'VIP')

!

NOT — reverses the result

!Confirmed

Real SAP Business One examples:

// Large orders from external customers
DocTotal > 5000 && !CONTAINS(CardCode, 'INT_')

// Notify for high-value OR urgent orders
DocTotal > 10000 || DocDueDate - DocDate < 3

// Only if confirmed and above threshold
Confirmed == true && DocTotal >= 2000

Parenthesis Operators

Parentheses control evaluation order, just like in math. Operations inside parentheses are evaluated first.

// Without parentheses: AND binds tighter, this means:
// DocTotal > 5000 AND (CardCode == 'A' OR CardCode == 'B')  ← NOT this
// (DocTotal > 5000 AND CardCode == 'A') OR CardCode == 'B'  ← this

// With parentheses: explicit control
DocTotal > 5000 && (CardCode == 'A' || CardCode == 'B')

// Another example: overdue AND (large OR VIP)
DocDueDate < TODAY() && (DocTotal > 10000 || CONTAINS(CardCode, 'VIP'))

When in doubt about precedence, add parentheses. They make your intent clear to anyone reading the formula later.

Arithmetic Operators

Standard math operations.

Operator

Meaning

Example

+

Addition

Quantity + ReturnsQty

-

Subtraction

DocTotal - VatSum

*

Multiplication

Quantity * UnitPrice

/

Division

DocTotal / Quantity

Real SAP Business One examples:

// Net amount after discount
DocTotal - (DocTotal * Discount / 100) > 1000

// Average unit price exceeds threshold
DocTotal / Quantity > 500

// Tax amount exceeds 10% of total
VatSum / DocTotal > 0.10

Overloaded + and - Operators

The + and - operators behave differently depending on the types they operate on.

String concatenation with +

When used with strings, + concatenates them:

// Build a composite lookup key
CardCode + '-' + DocNum

// Check if a constructed string matches a pattern
LEFT(CardCode, 2) + UPPER(DocCurrency) == 'USUSD'

If one side is a number and the other is a string, the number is silently converted to a string:

// Evaluates to 'REF-91'
'REF-' + DocEntry   →   'REF-91'

Date arithmetic with + and -

Dates are treated as day counts. Adding or subtracting an integer shifts the date by that many days:

// True if the order is due within 7 days of creation
DocDueDate - DocDate < 7

// True if the order's due date is more than 30 days from today
DocDueDate - TODAY() > 30

// True if an invoice is overdue (past due date)
TODAY() > DocDueDate

// Compare against a calculated future date
DocDueDate <= TODAY() + 14

The result of subtracting two dates is an integer number of days.

Time arithmetic with + and -

Times are treated as second counts. Adding or subtracting shifts the time by that many seconds:

// True if duration exceeds 1 hour (3600 seconds)
EndTime - StartTime > 3600

// True if activity ends after 5 PM
EndTime > TIME(17, 0, 0)

// True if something starts within the next 30 minutes from now
StartTime - NOW() < 1800

The result of subtracting two TIME values is an integer number of seconds.

String Functions

UPPER(text) and LOWER(text)

Convert text to all uppercase or all lowercase. Useful for case-insensitive comparisons.

// Case-insensitive country comparison
UPPER(Country) == 'DE'

// Normalise and compare
LOWER(CardCode) == LOWER('C20000')

CONTAINS(text, search)

Returns true if text contains search as a substring. Case-sensitive.

// Notify only for corporate customers (CardCode starts with 'CORP')
CONTAINS(CardCode, 'CORP')

// Notify for comments mentioning urgent delivery
CONTAINS(Comments, 'urgent')

// Notify for orders to specific region (CardCode convention)
CONTAINS(CardCode, '-EU-')

TRIM(text)

Removes leading and trailing spaces. Useful when data quality is uncertain.

// Safely compare even if there are extra spaces
TRIM(CardCode) == 'C20000'

LEN(text)

Returns the length of the string.

// Notify only if there is a comment (non-empty)
LEN(TRIM(Comments)) > 0

// Notify if reference number has the expected length
LEN(NumAtCard) == 10

LEFT(text, n) and RIGHT(text, n)

Extract characters from the start or end of a string.

// Notify only for orders from German customers (CardCode starts with 'DE')
LEFT(CardCode, 2) == 'DE'

// Check last 3 characters of a field
RIGHT(ItemCode, 3) == 'KIT'

MID(text, start, length)

Extract a substring starting at position start (1-indexed) with length characters.

// Extract the country code from a composite code like 'US-CUST-001'
MID(CardCode, 1, 2) == 'US'

// Extract middle segment of a code
MID(ItemCode, 4, 3) == 'RAW'

SUBSTITUTE(text, old, new)

Replace all occurrences of old with new in text.

// Normalise a code that might use dashes or underscores
SUBSTITUTE(CardCode, '_', '-') == 'CORP-001'

Date Functions

DATE(year, month, day)

Creates a date literal. Use this to compare against specific dates without relying on string comparisons.

// Notify for orders due after a specific campaign launch
DocDueDate >= DATE(2026, 10, 1)

// Notify for orders from a specific date range
DocDate >= DATE(2026, 9, 1) && DocDate < DATE(2026, 10, 1)

TODAY()

Returns the current local date value on the client machine at evaluation time. This is not necessarily the date on the database server, since the DB server may be installed on a different machine from the Service Layer or the SAP Business One desktop client.

// Notify for overdue orders
DocDueDate < TODAY()

// Notify for orders due within the next 5 days
DocDueDate >= TODAY() && DocDueDate <= TODAY() + 5

// Notify only for orders created today
DocDate == TODAY()

YEAR(date), MONTH(date), DAY(date)

Extract components of a date.

// Notify only for Q4 orders
MONTH(DocDate) >= 10

// Notify only for year-end orders
MONTH(DocDate) == 12 && DAY(DocDate) >= 25

// Notify for orders from a specific year
YEAR(DocDate) == 2026

// These functions also work on string dates in YYYYMMDD format
YEAR('20261001') == 2026

Time Functions

TIME(hours, minutes, seconds)

Creates a time literal using 24-hour clock.

// Notify for activities starting after 6 PM
StartTime >= TIME(18, 0, 0)

// Notify for early-morning activities (before 8 AM)
StartTime < TIME(8, 0, 0)

NOW()

Returns the current local date-time value on the client machine at evaluation time. This is not necessarily the date-time on the database server, since the DB server may be installed on a different machine from the Service Layer or the SAP Business One desktop client.

// Notify for activities starting within the next hour
StartTime >= NOW() && StartTime <= NOW() + 3600

// Notify for activities that started in the past
StartTime < NOW()

HOUR(time), MINUTE(time), SECOND(time)

Extract components of a time value.

// Only during business hours (9 AM to 5 PM)
HOUR(StartTime) >= 9 && HOUR(StartTime) < 17

// Only for activities at the top of the hour
MINUTE(StartTime) == 0

Math Functions

ABS(number)

Absolute value — removes the sign.

// Notify when discount deviation exceeds 5% in either direction
ABS(Discount - StandardDiscount) > 5

// Notify when quantity variance is significant
ABS(Quantity - OrderedQuantity) > 10

FLOOR(number) and CEILING(number)

Round down or up to the nearest integer.

// Compare rounded values
FLOOR(DocTotal / 1000) >= 10

// Notify when ceiling of unit price is above threshold
CEILING(UnitPrice) > 100

ROUND(number)

Round to the nearest integer.

// Notify when rounded total crosses a threshold
ROUND(DocTotal) > 5000

MIN(a, b, ...) and MAX(a, b, ...)

Smallest or largest value in a set.

// Notify when discount is above the max allowed
Discount > MAX(StandardDiscount, PartnerDiscount)

// Notify when price falls below the minimum
UnitPrice < MIN(StandardPrice, PromotionalPrice)

Logical Functions

IFNULL(expression, fallback)

Returns expression if it is not null, otherwise returns fallback. Useful for fields that might not be set.

// Treat null discount as 0 when comparing
IFNULL(Discount, 0) > 5

// Treat null comments as empty string when checking length
LEN(IFNULL(Comments, '')) > 0

// Use fallback currency for comparison
IFNULL(DocCurrency, 'USD') == 'EUR'

App-Level Variables

App-level variables give access to system context at evaluation time. They use the app. prefix.

app.CurrentUser

The login code of the user whose action triggered the event.

// Notify when a specific user creates a large order
// (useful for monitoring a trainee account)
app.CurrentUser == 'trainee01' && DocTotal > 1000

// Do NOT notify when the system account creates records (e.g. imports)
app.CurrentUser != 'System'

// Notify only when a manager creates or approves
app.CurrentUser == 'manager' || CONTAINS(app.CurrentUser, '_mgr')

app.CurrentCompany

The display name of the company database where the event occurred. Relevant when one endpoint receives events from multiple companies.

// Only process events from the production company
CONTAINS(app.CurrentCompany, 'Production')

// Route differently based on company
app.CurrentCompany == 'OEC Computers US'

app.Name

The process name of the application that triggered the event. This tells you which SAP Business One component caused the event.

app.Name value

What triggered the event

'SAP Business One'

SAP Business One Desktop Client

'httpd'

Service Layer (REST API call)

// Only notify for events created via Service Layer API (not desktop)
app.Name == 'httpd'

// Only notify for events created through the desktop client
app.Name == 'SAP Business One'

This is powerful for scenarios like: "send a notification to the integration team only when a user (not an API) creates an order above threshold — API-created orders are already handled by the source system."

app.VersionStr

The version of SAP Business One.

// Mostly useful for debugging or conditional logic during upgrades
app.VersionStr == '10.00.340'

app.OS

The operating system SAP Business One is running on. Returns 'WIN' or 'LINUX'.

Real-World Filter Expression Recipes

Here are complete, practical filter expressions for common SAP Business One integration scenarios.

Only large, confirmed sales orders from external customers:

DocTotal > 10000 && Confirmed == true && !CONTAINS(CardCode, 'INTERNAL')

Invoices overdue by more than 30 days:

TODAY() - DocDueDate > 30 && Status != 'bost_Close'

Business partner updates during business hours, not from automated imports:

HOUR(NOW()) >= 8 && HOUR(NOW()) < 18 && app.Name == 'SAP Business One'

Orders with urgent delivery comments:

CONTAINS(UPPER(Comments), 'URGENT') || DocDueDate - TODAY() <= 2

Activities assigned to a specific group of users:

CONTAINS(HandledBy, 'sales_') || HandledBy == 'manager'

High-value orders created via API (for downstream ERP sync):

DocTotal >= 5000 && app.Name == 'httpd'

Orders with non-standard payment terms (deviation monitoring):

PaymentGroupCode != ExpectedPaymentGroupCode && DocTotal > 1000

4. Putting It All Together: A Complete Advanced Subscription

Here is a production-ready subscription that uses HMAC auth, handshake, enriched payloads, and smart filtering:

POST /b1s/v2/EventSubscriptions

{
    "WebhookID": "HighValueOrdersSync",
    "WebhookURL": "https://erp-integration.partner.com/webhook/b1/orders",
    "AuthenticationType": "HMAC",
    "AuthenticationCred": "{\"Key\": \"kL8Xm2pQ9wZ3nV5jY7cB1tH4rE6uI0sD\", \"Algorithm\": \"HMACSha256\"}",
    "Handshake": "tYES",
    "VerifyCertificate": "tYES",
    "EventCollection": [
        {
            "BusinessObject": "Orders",
            "TransactionType": "Created",
            "BizObjProps": "DocEntry, CardCode, CardName, DocTotal, DocCurrency, DocDate, DocDueDate, Comments, SalesPersonCode",
            "FilterExpr": "DocTotal > 5000 && app.Name == 'httpd'"
        },
        {
            "BusinessObject": "Orders",
            "TransactionType": "Cancelled",
            "BizObjProps": "DocEntry, CardCode, DocTotal",
            "FilterExpr": "DocTotal > 5000"
        },
        {
            "BusinessObject": "BusinessPartners",
            "TransactionType": "Updated",
            "BizObjProps": "CardCode, CardName, Phone1, EmailAddress, Currency",
            "FilterExpr": "CardType == 'cCustomer'"
        }
    ]
}

This single subscription:

  • Notifies when large orders (>€5,000) are created via API, with full header data included
  • Notifies when such orders are subsequently cancelled
  • Notifies when customer business partners (not vendors or leads) are updated
  • Uses HMAC to verify every delivery is genuinely from SAP Business One
  • Uses handshake to verify the endpoint on creation and after any resume

5. Production Best Practices

This section covers the patterns and practices that separate a demo integration from one that runs reliably at scale in production.

Idempotency: Handle Duplicate Deliveries Gracefully

The Webhook Messenger guarantees at-least-once delivery — not exactly-once. Due to network conditions, retries, or timing edge cases, your endpoint may receive the same notification more than once.

Your handler must be idempotent: processing the same event twice produces the same result as processing it once.

Pattern: track processed event IDs in a database

async function handleEvent(event) {
    const eventId = event.id;

    // Check if we already processed this event
    const alreadyProcessed = await db.query(
        'SELECT 1 FROM processed_webhook_events WHERE event_id = $1',
        [eventId]
    );

    if (alreadyProcessed.rows.length > 0) {
        console.log(`[Idempotency] Skipping duplicate event: ${eventId}`);
        return;
    }

    // Record as processed BEFORE doing the work
    // This prevents concurrent duplicate processing
    await db.query(
        'INSERT INTO processed_webhook_events (event_id, processed_at) VALUES ($1, NOW())',
        [eventId]
    );

    // Do the actual work
    await processOrderCreation(event);
}

Table schema:

CREATE TABLE processed_webhook_events (
    event_id    VARCHAR(100) PRIMARY KEY,
    processed_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Clean up old entries periodically (events older than 30 days)
CREATE INDEX idx_processed_at ON processed_webhook_events (processed_at);

Clean up old entries: Set a periodic job to delete entries older than your MessageRetentionTime (default 30 days). Event IDs from older notifications will never be re-delivered.

Respond First, Process Second

Never do heavy work inside the HTTP request handler before returning. The Messenger has a 10-second timeout. If processing takes longer than that, the Messenger sees a timeout and retries — causing duplicate deliveries and growing your retry queue.

Pattern: acknowledge immediately, then queue for processing

Using a queue (Redis + Bull, RabbitMQ, AWS SQS, etc.):

const Queue = require('bull');
const webhookQueue = new Queue('webhook-events', { redis: { host: 'localhost' } });

app.post('/webhook/orders', verifyHmacSignature, (req, res) => {
    // Respond to SAP Business One immediately
    res.sendStatus(200);

    // Queue events for background processing
    const events = req.body;
    for (const event of events) {
        webhookQueue.add(event, {
            attempts: 3,         // Retry failed processing up to 3 times
            backoff: 5000,       // Wait 5s between retries
            removeOnComplete: true
        });
    }
});

// Worker processes events from the queue
webhookQueue.process(async (job) => {
    const event = job.data;
    await handleEvent(event);
});

If you are not using a message queue, at minimum use setImmediate() or process.nextTick() to defer processing after the response is sent.

High Availability for Your Endpoint

The Messenger deactivates a subscription that repeatedly fails to deliver. If your endpoint has a single point of failure (one server, no redundancy), a server crash moves your subscription to Inactive state. You then need to:

  1. Fix the server
  2. Manually call the Resume API
  3. Optionally replay missed events

A better approach is to design for availability so outages are rare and brief:

Load balancing: Run multiple instances of your webhook endpoint behind a load balancer. If one instance crashes, the others keep serving.

Health checks: Configure your load balancer to health-check each endpoint instance. Remove unhealthy instances from rotation automatically.

Auto-restart: Use a process manager (PM2, systemd, Kubernetes) to restart crashed processes automatically.

Graceful shutdown: When deploying a new version, drain in-flight requests before stopping the old instance to prevent losing notifications during deployment.

SSL Certificate Management

Use a certificate from a trusted CA in production. Let's Encrypt provides free, auto-renewing certificates that are trusted by the Messenger's default trust store.

Set up automatic renewal. Certificates expire. If your certificate expires, the Messenger starts rejecting your endpoint and deactivating subscriptions. Use certbot or a managed certificate service that renews automatically.

Monitor certificate expiry. Add an alert that fires 30 days before your certificate expires. Some monitoring services (Datadog, New Relic, UptimeRobot) can do this automatically for HTTPS endpoints.

For self-signed certs in development: Import the certificate into the Messenger's trust store using the import tool. The alternative — setting VerifyCertificate: tNO — is fine for development but must be changed to tYES before go-live.

Logging and Observability

Your webhook endpoint should produce structured logs that let you answer:

  • Did we receive this event?
  • Did we process it successfully?
  • How long did processing take?
  • Which events did we skip (duplicates)?

Minimum log fields per event:

async function processEvents(events) {
    for (const event of events) {
        const startTime = Date.now();

        logger.info({
            eventId: event.id,
            eventType: event.type,
            subject: event.subject,
            source: event.source,
            receivedAt: new Date().toISOString()
        }, 'Processing webhook event');

        try {
            await handleEvent(event);

            logger.info({
                eventId: event.id,
                durationMs: Date.now() - startTime
            }, 'Event processed successfully');

        } catch (err) {
            logger.error({
                eventId: event.id,
                error: err.message,
                stack: err.stack,
                durationMs: Date.now() - startTime
            }, 'Event processing failed');
        }
    }
}

Correlate with SAP Business One EventNotifications: The event.id in your logs is the same as the EventID in SAP Business One's EventNotifications entity. When investigating a support ticket, you can query both your logs and SAP Business One's event log using the same ID.

Scaling for High Event Volume

If your SAP Business One company generates thousands of events per minute, a few settings need careful tuning:

MessageBatchLimit: A higher batch limit means fewer HTTP calls but larger payloads per call. Match this to your endpoint's capacity. If your endpoint can handle 500 events per request in under 1 second, set it to 500. If it struggles with more than 50, set it lower.

Parallel processing in your endpoint: If you receive a batch of 200 events, you do not have to process them sequentially. Use Promise.all() or a concurrency-limited batch processor:

const pLimit = require('p-limit');

async function processEvents(events) {
    const limit = pLimit(10); // Process up to 10 events in parallel

    await Promise.all(events.map(event =>
        limit(() => handleEvent(event).catch(err => {
            logger.error({ eventId: event.id, err }, 'Event processing error');
        }))
    ));
}

Database connection pooling: If your event handler writes to a database, use a connection pool sized appropriately for your maximum concurrency. A pool of 10 connections with 10-parallel event processing means each event gets its own connection with no waiting.

6. Troubleshooting Runbook

Use this as a systematic guide when things go wrong.

Subscription went Inactive

Symptoms: Subscription State is "Inactive". Notifications stopped arriving.

Investigation steps:

  1. Query EventNotifications for recent failures:
GET /b1s/v2/EventNotifications?$filter=Status eq 'Failed'&$orderby=CreateDate desc&$top=10
  1. If using FP 2608+, check DeliveryDetails in the response for the specific HTTP error code
  2. Test your endpoint manually: curl -k -X POST https://your-app/webhook -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '[{"id":"test"}]'
  3. Check your endpoint's logs for errors around the time notifications stopped

Common causes and fixes:

Cause

Fix

Endpoint returned 5xx repeatedly

Fix the error in your endpoint code, then Resume

Endpoint timed out (>10s)

Move processing to async, then Resume

SSL certificate expired

Renew certificate, then Resume

Firewall blocked the Messenger

Open the firewall rule, then Resume

Endpoint URL changed

Delete the subscription and recreate it with the new URL, then ensure the new endpoint passes the handshake

After fixing the root cause:

POST /b1s/v2/EventSubscriptions('YourWebhookID')/Resume

Handshake failing during subscription creation

Symptoms: POST to EventSubscriptions returns an error like "Handshake failed".

Checklist:

  • Your endpoint is running and accessible from the SAP Business One server (not just your laptop)
  • Your endpoint handles GET requests (not only POST)
  • Your endpoint reads X-B1-Webhook-Token from the request headers
  • Your endpoint returns {"Challenge": "<the-token>"} with Content-Type: application/json
  • Your endpoint responds within 10 seconds
  • Your SSL certificate is valid (or imported if self-signed)
  • No firewall between SAP Business One server and your endpoint blocks HTTPS
  • If using HMAC auth, the signature verification in your handshake handler is correct

Quick test: Call the handshake API manually after setting Handshake: "tNO" during creation, then troubleshoot with the manual endpoint:

POST /b1s/v2/EventSubscriptions('YourWebhookID')/Handshake

Cannot enable webhooks (error 10001237)

See Section 4 of Part 1. Set ExcelFolderPath and XMLFileFolderPath to empty strings in the same CompanyService_UpdateAdminInfo call.

Webhook Messenger is not reachable

Test:

telnet {your-b1-server} 40008

If connection refused or timed out:

  • The Webhook Messenger Service may not be installed
  • The service may be stopped — check Windows Services or the Linux service manager
  • Firewall may be blocking port 40008

Contact your SAP Business One system administrator to verify installation and firewall rules.

Duplicate notifications being processed

Symptom: Your downstream system shows duplicate records.

Cause: Your endpoint is not implementing idempotency, or the idempotency check is not working.

Fix: Implement the database-backed idempotency pattern shown in Section 5. Use event.id as the unique key.

Also check: Is your endpoint returning 200 reliably? If it sometimes returns 5xx (or times out), the Messenger retries, sending the same event again.

7. FAQ

Q: When does the Messenger retry a delivery?

Retry occurs on HTTP 5xx, 408, 429, and network-level failures (timeout, DNS failure, connection refused). It does not retry on 4xx except 408 and 429.

Q: Will notifications always arrive in the order events occurred?

Within a single company, yes — the Messenger attempts in-order delivery. If you have one webhook subscribed to events from multiple companies, ordering across companies is not guaranteed. Design your handler to tolerate out-of-order delivery (e.g. use the time field on the event rather than assuming sequence).

Q: Can the same event trigger notifications to multiple webhooks?

Yes. If two subscriptions both watch Orders.Created, SAP Business One creates one EventNotification record and the Messenger delivers it to both webhook endpoints. The DeliveryDetails collection on the notification record tracks delivery status per webhook.

Q: What happens if my endpoint is slow and events pile up?

Events accumulate in the Messenger's in-memory queue. As long as the queue has capacity, events wait and are eventually delivered. If the queue is full, the Messenger waits for space before accepting new events — this creates back-pressure. For sustained high volume, batch processing (MessageBatchLimit) and a fast, non-blocking endpoint are essential.

Q: Can I use FilterExpr to subscribe to events from specific users only?

Yes. Use app.CurrentUser:

app.CurrentUser == 'salesmanager' || CONTAINS(app.CurrentUser, '_senior')

Q: How do I handle multi-company scenarios (one endpoint, multiple databases)?

Use the source field in the notification payload to identify which company triggered the event:

"source": "/default/sap.b1/COMPANYDB_NAME"

Parse the database name from the source and route accordingly.

Q: Is there a limit on the number of properties in BizObjProps?

There is no documented hard limit, but be practical. Each property adds to the payload size. Stick to properties your integration actually needs. Avoid large text fields (e.g. long memo fields) that bloat the payload without adding value.

Q: Can I change BizObjProps or FilterExpr on an existing subscription without deleting it?

Yes. Use PATCH with B1S-ReplaceCollectionsOnPatch: true to replace the entire EventCollection with updated entries:

PATCH /b1s/v2/EventSubscriptions('HighValueOrdersSync')
B1S-ReplaceCollectionsOnPatch: true

{
    "EventCollection": [
        {
            "BusinessObject": "Orders",
            "TransactionType": "Created",
            "BizObjProps": "DocEntry, CardCode, DocTotal, DocDueDate",
            "FilterExpr": "DocTotal > 8000"
        }
    ]
}

entry.title: UDV Event-Based Triggering
entry.content:
SAP Business One 10.0 FP 2608 brings a nice enhancement to User-Defined Values (UDV): a new way to trigger a formula based on events.

If you've worked with UDV formulas (mathematical or logical), you know that for a formula to run automatically, you need to define a trigger – a field on the form that, when changed by the user, activates the formula and populates the target field.

This works well in many cases. But what if you want the formula to run when the user clicks ‘Add’ or ‘Update’, rather than when a specific field changes? Before FP 2608, that wasn't possible.

FP 2608 introduces two new triggering options:

- On events – the formula runs automatically when the document is Added or Updated. No trigger field needed.

- On field changes or events – a combined mode: the formula runs both when a trigger field changes or when the document is Added or Updated.

The existing trigger on field change only is still available.

Example: assume you have a UDF called 'Last Modified By' on a sales order, and you want it to always store the name of the user who last saved the document. With the new events option, the formula simply runs on every Add or Update.

For more details, refer to the online help.

This is a small but impactful change - it lets UDV formulas respond to the most natural user action: adding or saving a document.

entry.title: Defining UDV for Horizontal Fields
entry.content:
The latest version of SAP Business One Web Client 10.0 FP 2608 introduces a powerful enhancement to User-Defined Values: you can now assign a UDV to a specific field even when multiple fields share the same label.

Background: In SAP Business One Web Client, it's common for two or more controls to sit under a single label or section header – for example, Email and Fax checkboxes in Business Partner form. Until now, if you wanted to assign a UDV to one of those fields, it was not possible since the system couldn't clearly indicate which field had the assignment – the orange brackets [] used as the UDV indicator were placed at the label level, so when multiple fields shared that label, there was no way to tell which one was actually linked to a UDV.

To fully support such case, we redesigned the indicator. The orange brackets have been replaced with a dedicated new icon – a standard Fiori icon that intuitively signals a value has been customized by the user.

 With this new icon design:

- The icon is placed next to each individual field, not at the label level

- In object edit mode, the icon appears as greyed-out, serving as a non-interactive visual indicator that the field is linked to a UDV

- In UDV edit mode, the same icon turns blue, indicating it's clickable, so you can access and modify the UDV definition

Example:

When you enter Business Partner Edit mode, you will see the following icons appearance :

The ‘Sales Employees’ field as well as ‘Email’ and ‘Fax’ checkboxes are defined with UDV.

When you enter UDV Edit mode, you will see the following icons appearance:

Since 'Remarks' has no UDV defined yet, you’ll see a special icon, blue pencil, so when clicking it, you can create a UDV for it.

You can toggle the UDV indicator visibility in your user profile settings under the Display UDV Indicator option.

Note that this switch applies only for Edit mode – no indication in View mode.
